Subject: LumenHealth - order form redlines (IP & training concerns)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal reviewed the draft order form and pulled a few redlines we need to discuss before signature. The primary items are:

- Output ownership: we need explicit assignment of product output/title for customer-generated prompts (we plan to embed results in our product).
- Training / data use: no model retraining or use of our prompts/logs for model improvement without opt-in and explicit data minimization guarantees.
- Feedback license: if Redwood wants to use anonymized examples for tuning, we need narrow, non-exclusive, revocable license language and carveouts for any PII or PHI.

I attached our marked order form (LumenHealth_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.docx) and a short questionnaire from legal. Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to:
1) accept assignment of output/title for customer prompts, or provide an equivalent commercial mechanism?
2) agree to a strict opt-in training scope and an evidence checklist we can audit (logs, telemetry definitions)?

We'd like to get to a signed order form within the next two weeks — procurement has a weekly cadence on Fridays. If it's easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to align.

Thanks,
Sasha Ivanov
Senior Procurement Manager

Subject: Re: LumenHealth - order form redlines (IP & training concerns)

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the specificity, that helps a lot. Summary of where we can land and proposed path:

1) Output ownership: we are comfortable with customer assignment of output/title for customer-supplied prompts and generated content used solely by LumenHealth internally or in your products. We propose explicit language in the order form that assigns output rights for Customer Content and Generated Output, with a limited license back to Redwood solely to operate and monitor the service (no downstream commercialization).

2) Training / data use: we can offer an opt-in training workflow. By default Redwood will NOT use LumenHealth prompts/logs to retrain models. If you opt in, the agreement will require:
   - explicit selection (checkbox in onboarding or signed addendum)
   - data minimization and automated PII/PHI redaction steps
   - ability to revoke opt-in with a 30-day notice and evidence of data deletion where applicable

3) Feedback license: we can accept a narrow, non-exclusive, revocable license for anonymized feedback used only for model quality improvements. Carveouts: no PII/PHI, no export of identifiable customer data to third parties. We will include telemetry definitions and examples in the addendum.

Next steps I suggest: Redwood legal prepares a one-page addendum that enumerates the opt-in mechanism and telemetry/evidence items (logs schema, retention window, deletion procedure). I'll attach a starter addendum and a redlined order form (Redwood_Addendum_Draft_vA.pdf). If that looks good to you, we can route to your legal/procurement and aim for signature.

Proposed timeline: draft addendum by Wed (6/23), internal legal review Thu-Fri, sign next week. If you prefer a call, I can do Tue or Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Folks — looping legal counsel (I’ll introduce after we agree to language). Quick notes to include in the addendum / order form:

- Concrete defs: define "Customer Content", "Generated Output", "Anonymized Feedback", and "Telemetry". Keep Generated Output assignment scoped to outputs produced from Customer Content only.
- Operational carveouts: explicit exclusion for PII/PHI; define redaction approach (automated + manual review for exceptions).
- Revocation: opt-in must be revocable with 30 days notice and a requirement that any retained training artifacts derived from LumenHealth data be deleted/rotated out of active training datasets within a defined window.
- Evidence items: sample log schema (fields + retention), deletion confirmation process, SOC2 evidence pointer, and a contact for data subject requests.
- Procurement ask: procurement will want a permitted-use box in the order form and a signature flow separate from product purchases. Suggest we include an exec approval skip clause for small pilots (< 100k tokens/month).

I suggest we include the following language snippets in the addendum (we'll refine with legal):
1) "Customer retains ownership of Generated Output; Redwood receives a limited, non-transferable license to use Generated Output solely to provide the Service."
2) "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Generated Output to train models unless Customer opts in via signed addendum; opt-in is revocable with 30 days notice."
3) "Anonymized Feedback: Redwood may use strictly anonymized, non-identifiable examples for quality improvement; Redwood will not retain any PII/PHI and will provide deletion evidence upon request."

Rafael — can you confirm if the pilot exemption box is acceptable commercially? Ben — I'll need you to draft the procurement note for signature flow. I’ll prep the legal intro and a one-pager evidence checklist to attach to the addendum.
